title: Gullwing Telecom partner play scratchpad
body:
One-line objective:
Test Redwood Dedicated and Optimize with Gullwing to surface a repeatable product-led pilot for network diagnostics assistants and internal NOC automation. Goal: 3-month pilot, measurable latency improvement for inference calls in their on-prem environment and 20% reduction in per-call cost vs. their current managed endpoint stack.

Context / account summary:
- Company: Gullwing Telecom (mid-sized regional carrier, ~3k employees, sizable B2B enterprise accounts).
- Why now: recently spun up a NOC automation program; public posts about ML adoption in operations; procurement RFP for 'AI observability' closed Q3.
- Tech posture: hybrid cloud + on-prem PoPs, strict data residency for customer traffic; currently running vendor-managed endpoints (vendor X) + some internal TF Serving workloads.
- Financial: CFO memo mentions wanting to cut 25% of per-ticket handling cost in ops by FY27.

Key contacts (unverified emails):
- Lena Ortiz — Head of Platform (platform+infra), likely the primary technical champion.
- Marcus Hsu — CTO, cares about SLAs and vendor lock-in.
- Darrin Cole — VP Product, owns NOC automation roadmap.
- Sophie Patel — Procurement lead (controls contracts >$50k).

Stakes / value props to emphasize:
- Private deployments and VPC control: matches their residency and compliance needs (no egress of traffic).
- Dedicated pools for predictable throughput: NOC queries are latency-sensitive during incidents.
- Optimize recommendations + caching: immediate unit-cost wins on repeated diagnostic prompts.
- Rollout and fallback policies: reduce risk in integrating LLMs into incident workflows.

Suggested pilot (sketch):
- Duration: 12 weeks (3 months)
- Scope: migrate 2 diagnostic workflows from vendor X to Redwood Dedicated in their private datacenter (one low-complexity template + one medium complexity contextual prompt).
- Success metrics: median inference latency < 250ms at p95 under synthetic NOC traffic; token cost per query <= current baseline * 0.8; no incidents caused by model degradations; operator satisfaction >= +0.3 NPS change on sample.
- Offer: pilot credits for infra ($25k) + 2 weeks of solutions-engineering support; reduced PoC rate for on-prem connector work.

High-level technical notes (for eng convo):
- Need to map their PoPs, network egress limitations, and whether HSM/KMS integration required.
- Likely hardware: they have spare A100 hosts in two PoPs (east/west), maybe amenable to Dedicated but procurement prefers Redwood-hosted Private control plane with customer-managed infra.
- Integration surface: REST API + streaming for NOC console; must support low-latency short-turnaround calls with prefix caching; offline model variant fallback for capacity spikes.

Outreach plan / cadence (initial sequence):
1) Intro email to Lena (personalized, 1-2 short lines about NOC automation + Redwood private options)
2) 3-day follow-up: share short 1-pager + proposed 12-week pilot outline
3) If interest, ask for 30–45m techncial sync w/ platform + NOC SMEs; include solutions eng and an SRE to talk latency/workload profiling
4) Procurement engagement once a technical greenlight (aim for term sheet + statement of work within 6 weeks of sync)

Draft email (subject ideas):
- Subject A: "Reduce NOC diagnostic latency — pilot idea for Gullwing"
- Body (short): Hi Lena — quick note: saw Gullwing's post about NOC automation. We helped several telcos move operational workflows to private inference with predictable latencies and lower token cost. Would love to share a 12-week pilot that keeps data in your PoPs and aims to lower per-query cost by ~20%. Can you point me to the right person on platform? — Maya

Call skeleton (technical sync):
- 5m intros, 10m NOC use-case walk-through by them, 15m runtime/ops discussion (batching, caching, fallback), 10m pilot logistics + success metrics, 5m next steps.

Objections + suggested responses:
- "We can't open up our PoPs to vendors": Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking and on-prem package; control plane can be run privately and keys remain in customer KMS. Offer architecture diagram and reference checklist.
- "Token costs are unpredictable": show Optimize suggestions, caching, and dedicated pooling math; propose a short cost profiling run using anonymized sample logs.
- "We already have a vendor X contract": offer a short comparative pilot; emphasize low-risk (short duration, limited scope) and migration path with rollback policies.
- "Procurement requires SOC2/ISO docs": provide our compliance artifacts and point to enterprise package.

Quick ROI sketch (very rough):
- Assumptions: avg NOC diagnostic consumes 120 tokens, current vendor cost equivalent $0.025 per diagnostic. 100k diagnostics/month.
- Current monthly spend: $2,500.
- Target: 20% cost reduction -> $2,000/mo -> $500/mo savings; annualized ~$6k.
- Note: this is conservative and omits operator time saved from speed improvements.

Open questions / data to collect from them:
- Realistic QPS and burst patterns for NOC queries (p95 latency targets they define).
- Whether training data or logs must remain on-prem (PII/telemetry concerns).
- Existing vendor contract end-date and migration constraints.
- KMS/HSM vendor and key rotation policies.

Next immediate actions (owner tags):
- Maya: update pilot one-pager with concrete SOW bullets + estimated SE hours (Due: 2026-03-17).
- Elliot: validate A100 availability and suggested Dedicated sizing for 250ms p95 target (Due: 2026-03-18).
- Priya: draft procurement brief and attach SOC2/ISO artifacts; pre-fill common terms to speed procurement (Due: 2026-03-19).
- Ask Lena for initial 30m sync — aim for week of 2026-03-24.

Misc notes / rapid brainstorms:
- Low-friction demo: deploy a tiny on-prem connector that proxies to a Redwood Dedicated pool in their test PoP; demo must show p95 numbers and quick cost delta.
- Alternative quick win: offer hosted evaluation of non-sensitive sample queries to show token-cost delta before on-prem work.
- Success story to cite: generic telco-case (anonymized) that saved ~18% on per-call cost and reduced mean operator response time by 1.2x.

Notes-to-self: keep tone mild, emphasize choice (hosted vs private vs dedicated), not a hard sell. Additional collateral: short latency benchmark, 1-pager on Optimize, private-deployments checklist (link in linked_artifacts).

Unresolved / follow-up list:
- Need procurement thresholds for contract sign-off (> $50k requires legal review?). (Maya)
- Confirm if they require on-prem audit window (SLA-style monitoring) before pilot starts. (Elliot)
- Build short anonymized log transformer for cost profiling (Priya + solutions eng).
summary: Scratchpad for outbound and pilot planning for Gullwing Telecom. Focus on private/dedicated options, pilot outline, objections, next steps.
